title: Best Ace Hardware Dehumidifier (2026): Models Worth Buying
h1: The Best Ace Hardware Dehumidifiers (Plus Menards and Tractor Supply)
dek: Your local hardware store can get you a great dehumidifier — if you know which models to ask for and which shelf-fillers to skip.
description: The best Ace Hardware dehumidifier picks for basements, small rooms and cold spaces, plus what to know before buying one at Menards or Tractor Supply.
intro: Shopping for an **Ace Hardware dehumidifier** has one big advantage over clicking “buy” on a marketplace listing: you can walk in, lift the bucket, and ask someone who sells them every summer. The catch is that most Ace stores are independently owned, so the dehumidifiers on the floor vary a lot from town to town, and the full selection lives online with free pickup at your local store.

To make that easier, we picked the models we’d look for first — the same mainstream brands you’ll find at Ace, Menards and other hardware chains — and explained what separates a good buy from a shelf-filler. We also cover the regional alternatives, the coldest-running options for garages and crawl spaces, and how to get rid of your old unit responsibly.
topPicksLead: The **Frigidaire 50-Pint (FFAD5033W1)** is the best all-around choice for most basements: a full 50-pint machine with a set-a-number humidistat and a hose connection for hands-off draining.

products.name: Frigidaire 50-Pint Dehumidifier (FFAD5033W1)
pros: Full 50-pint capacity for basements and large rooms
Digital humidistat holds a set percentage
cons: Tall cabinet needs a clear spot
products.whyWeLoveIt: Frigidaire is one of the most widely stocked dehumidifier brands in American hardware and home stores, and this is the model in its range that suits the most homes. It has the capacity for a damp basement and the controls to hold a sensible 45–50% without babysitting.
products.performance: It’s a 50-pint compressor unit under the current DOE rating, which is the size most makers recommend for a damp basement or a large open room. Attach a garden-style hose and it drains continuously to a floor drain, so you’re not emptying a bucket twice a day in July. Owners like the straightforward controls and auto-restart after a power cut.
products.notes: See how it stacks up against the rest of the lineup in our [best Frigidaire dehumidifier](/best/best-frigidaire-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: Frigidaire 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Built-In Pump (FFAP5033W1)
pros: Built-in pump pushes water up to a sink or window
Same 50-pint capacity as our top pick
Works with pump, gravity hose or bucket
cons: Costs more than the non-pump version
Pump line needs an occasional check for kinks
products.whyWeLoveIt: If there’s no floor drain near where the dehumidifier needs to sit, the pump is the feature that makes it a set-and-forget appliance. It lifts water up and out to a laundry sink or through a window, so the unit can run all season untouched.
products.performance: It shares the same 50-pint compressor platform as the FFAD5033W1, adding a condensate pump. Owners consistently say the pump is what turned dehumidifying from a daily chore into something they forget about. Compare it with other self-draining models in our [dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) roundup.

specs.Drainage: Built-in pump, gravity hose or bucket

products.name: Honeywell TP50AWKN 50-Pint Dehumidifier
products.whyWeLoveIt: Honeywell is a familiar name on hardware-store shelves, and this 50-pint model covers the basics well for a little less. If you have a floor drain and just want a reliable box that holds a humidity level, it does the job.
products.performance: It’s a straightforward 50-pint-class compressor unit with a digital humidistat. Owners like the solid bucket handle and easy-to-read controls. Set it on a block or shelf so the drain hose runs downhill to the floor drain, and it can run all summer without emptying.

products.name: Midea 22-Pint ENERGY STAR Dehumidifier (MAD22C1AWS)
pros: Right-sized for bedrooms, offices and laundry rooms
Lighter and easier to move than a 50-pint unit
cons: Too small for a wet basement
Smaller bucket fills quickly in humid weeks
products.whyWeLoveIt: Not every room needs a basement-sized machine. This compact Midea covers a bedroom, home office or laundry room efficiently, and it’s the kind of size you can carry home from the store and set up in minutes.
products.performance: It’s rated at 22 pints a day under the 2019 DOE test — older labeling would have called it a 35-pint unit — and it’s ENERGY STAR certified, which helps when it runs most of the summer. For a small, moderately damp room it holds a set humidity without much fuss.

products.name: AlorAir Sentinel HD55 Crawl Space Dehumidifier
pros: Auto-defrost keeps it working down to about 36°F
cons: Usually an online order rather than a shelf item
products.whyWeLoveIt: Searching for the lowest-temperature dehumidifier usually means you’ve watched a regular portable ice up in a cool basement or crawl space. This AlorAir is built for exactly those conditions, and it’s worth ordering online if your hardware store doesn’t carry it.
products.performance: AlorAir rates it at 55 pints a day under AHAM conditions, with automatic defrost that keeps it running in spaces down to about 36°F. Water leaves through a gravity hose, so map your drain route before buying. More cold-space options are in our [crawl space dehumidifier](/best/best-crawl-space-dehumidifier/) guide.

blocks.text: We don’t run a lab. We focused on brands that mainstream hardware and home stores actually carry, then compared current 2019 DOE capacity ratings, ENERGY STAR listings, manuals (for drainage, humidistat type and operating range) and the CPSC recall database. Owner reviews filled in the rest: leaky buckets, failed pumps, compressors that quit after one season.

Because Ace stores stock different items, we didn’t pick based on what one store had on the floor. Every model here can be found through hardware retailers or ordered online, and the advice applies wherever you buy.

sections.heading: What to look for in an Ace Hardware dehumidifier

items.label: The DOE 2019 pint rating
items.text: Boxes and older listings sometimes use the pre-2019 rating, which makes a 35-pint unit sound like a 50. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) explains the switch.

items.label: A real humidistat
items.text: Choose a model where you set a percentage, not just Low and High. Aim for 45–50% in most homes.

items.label: A drainage plan
items.text: A gravity hose is perfect if there’s a floor drain. If not, a built-in pump saves you from emptying a bucket every day.

items.label: The right temperature range
items.text: Most portables are designed for living-space temperatures and can ice up in cool basements. For cold spaces, look for auto-defrost or a low-temp rating.

items.label: Warranty and recall history
items.text: Check the CPSC recall list for the model number, and keep your receipt — warranty claims usually go through the manufacturer, not the store.

sections.heading: Tips for buying a dehumidifier at Ace Hardware

items: **Check online first.** Ace’s website shows a bigger selection than any single store, and many items can be shipped to your local store for free pickup.
**Ask the store to order it.** Because stores are locally owned, staff can often bring in a specific model from the warehouse.
**Join Ace Rewards.** The free loyalty program earns points and member deals, which helps on a higher-ticket item.
**Shop the season.** Stock usually arrives in spring and sells down through summer; late-season clearance can be a good time to buy for next year.
**Ask about returns before you buy.** Return policies can vary by store, so confirm what happens if the unit arrives damaged or fails early.

blocks.title: Size it before you shop
blocks.text: A bedroom or office usually needs 20–30 pints, a damp basement 50. If you’re drying a basement, start at 50 pints — an undersized unit runs nonstop and still falls behind.

blocks.text: Whichever store you choose, the same rules apply: confirm the DOE pint rating, choose a set-percentage humidistat and plan the drainage. If you’re a warehouse-club member, our [Costco dehumidifier](/best/best-costco-dehumidifier/) guide covers that aisle too.

Ordinary portable dehumidifiers work best in rooms that are comfortable for people. As temperatures drop toward the 50s and below, their coils can frost over, water removal falls off and the unit spends more time defrosting. If yours keeps icing up, our [dehumidifier freezing up](/guides/dehumidifier-freezing-up/) guide walks through the fixes.

items: **Low-temp compressor units** like the AlorAir Sentinel HD55 use automatic defrost to keep working down to about 36°F — ideal for crawl spaces and cool basements.
**Desiccant dehumidifiers** don’t rely on a cold coil, so they keep working near freezing; see our [desiccant dehumidifier](/best/best-desiccant-dehumidifier/) picks for unheated garages and cabins.
**Standard portables** are the best value for conditioned spaces, and many have a low-temperature mode for basements that sit in the low 60s.

sections.heading: Shopping for an air purifier or humidifier at Menards, too?

blocks.text: Many people searching for a dehumidifier are also browsing air purifiers and humidifiers in the same aisle. They solve different problems: an air purifier filters dust, pollen and smoke but doesn’t touch humidity, and a humidifier adds moisture — the opposite of what a damp basement needs. Our [dehumidifier vs. air purifier](/guides/dehumidifier-vs-air-purifier/) guide explains when you need one, the other or both, and our [dehumidifier and air purifier combo](/best/best-dehumidifier-air-purifier-combo/) picks cover the all-in-one route.

Old dehumidifiers contain refrigerant, which federal rules require to be recovered by a certified technician before the unit is scrapped, so it shouldn’t just go out with the trash. Store take-back and haul-away policies vary by retailer and location — including at Home Depot and other big-box chains — so call ahead. Many local utilities and municipal recycling programs accept them too. Our [how to dispose of a dehumidifier](/guides/how-to-dispose-of-a-dehumidifier/) guide lists every option.

For most basements, ask your hardware store for the **Frigidaire FFAD5033W1**, or the **Frigidaire FFAP5033W1** if there’s no floor drain and you need a pump. The **Honeywell TP50AWKN** is a no-frills value alternative, the **Midea MAD22C1AWS** suits a single small room, and the **AlorAir Sentinel HD55** is worth ordering online if your space runs cold. Whatever you buy, check the DOE pint rating, choose a real humidistat and keep the receipt.

faqs.a: Yes. Many Ace stores stock dehumidifiers seasonally, and Ace’s website offers a wider range, often with free pickup at your local store. Because most stores are independently owned, the selection on the floor varies by location.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier at Ace Hardware?
faqs.a: For most basements, a 50-pint unit with a set-percentage humidistat and a drain-hose connection, such as the Frigidaire FFAD5033W1. If you have no floor drain, choose a pump model like the Frigidaire FFAP5033W1.

faqs.q: Can I return a dehumidifier to Ace Hardware?
faqs.a: Usually, but return policies can vary by store because most Ace locations are locally owned. Ask before you buy and keep your receipt; warranty repairs typically go through the manufacturer.
Yes, Menards stores typically carry room and basement dehumidifiers during the humid season. Look for a 50-pint DOE 2019 rating for a basement, and watch for the store’s 11% rebate promotions.
Tractor Supply carries a smaller selection, much of it online. It’s convenient if you’re already shopping there, but compare the model number against our picks before buying.

Desiccant dehumidifiers work closest to freezing because they don’t use a cold coil. Among compressor models, low-temp crawl space units with auto-defrost, such as the AlorAir Sentinel HD55, run down to about 36°F.
